Question: Derive the equations of motion for uniformly accelerated motion using velocity-time graphs.
reference_answer: From a v-t graph, acceleration a = (v - u)/t gives v = u + at. The area under the graph gives displacement s = ut + (1/2)at^2. Eliminating t gives v^2 = u^2 + 2as.
keywords: equations of motion, velocity-time graph, acceleration, displacement

Question: State and explain the law of conservation of energy with an example of a falling body.
reference_answer: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only transformed. For a falling body, potential energy mgh converts into kinetic energy (1/2)mv^2; neglecting air resistance, the total mechanical energy remains constant.
keywords: conservation of energy, potential energy, kinetic energy, mechanical energy

Question: Explain the first law of thermodynamics and apply it to an isothermal and an adiabatic process.
reference_answer: Delta Q = Delta U + Delta W. In an isothermal process temperature is constant, so Delta U = 0 and Q = W. In an adiabatic process Q = 0, so Delta U = -W and internal energy changes at the expense of work.
keywords: thermodynamics, first law, isothermal, adiabatic, internal energy, work

Question: Derive the expression for the effective resistance of two resistors connected in parallel.
reference_answer: For parallel resistors, the same potential difference V exists across both and current I = I1 + I2. Using I1 = V/R1 and I2 = V/R2 gives I = V(1/R1 + 1/R2), so 1/Reff = 1/R1 + 1/R2.
keywords: parallel resistors, effective resistance, current, potential difference
